title: Welcome Station Task-Train and 14D Curation
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, practical "Welcome Station" for new joiners — a 14-day curated task-train that combines technical setup, social rituals, and competency checkpoints. Designed to be terse enough for managers to follow and explicit enough for mentors to hand off.

Audience / scope:
- New ICs and first-level managers across engineering, product, and SRE joining in hybrid or remote locations.
- Focus on first 14 calendar days (with explicit pass-offs for 30/60/90).
- Not a replacement for detailed team runbooks; links to deeper artifacts included.

High-level principles (why this is different):
1) Task-train model: daily short missions vs long task lists — small wins build confidence.
2) Welcome Station: a single checklist the new joiner and mentor own together (not siloed by admin).
3) Competency-first handoffs: every milestone includes a lightweight signal to mark readiness.
4) Remote-first flex: rituals that work asynchronously (call windows, async intro threads).

Quick start (manager checklist before day 0):
- Confirm laptop order and provisioning SLA with infra (target: ship 5 business days prior).
- Assign primary mentor + secondary backup; confirm 30-min meet-times for week 1.
- Create Welcome Station doc for the hire (copy template).
- Open access tickets: email groups, slack channels, project repos, GA accounts.
- Prepare 3 very small starter issues/tasks labelled "welcome-starter".

14-day task-train (day-by-day missions) — condensed view:
Day 0 (pre-boarding): accept paperwork, confirm hardware shipping, Slack intro message drafted by manager.
Day 1: orientation ritual (30–45m), set status message, fill "workstation snapshot" (w/ local timezone, preferred hours). Complete HR forms.
Day 2: dev environment: clone repo + hello-world PR (mentor reviews). Join team standup.
Day 3: infra & access deep-check: validate CI run, access to tracked dashboards, billing read-only.
Day 4: pairing session on real bug or tiny feature. Deliverable: merged PR or documented follow-up.
Day 5: product-context session with PM (30m). Write 1-paragraph product perspective note.
Day 6: ops-oncall primer (read runbook + shadow pager replay).
Day 7: social async: post a learning note in #team-onboarding, schedule coffee with cross-functional buddy.
Day 8: independent small task from "welcome-starter" list; mentor evaluates via 3-point rubric.
Day 9: architecture walkthrough (60m) with recordings and annotated notes.
Day 10: security checklist (KMS/HSM access review if applicable).
Day 11: customer context — read 2 support tickets and write one-sentence improvement idea.
Day 12: end-to-end integration test run and fix minor flake.
Day 13: mentor-led feedback session (30m) and calibration against competency map.
Day 14: 14-day readout: new joiner presents "First Wins + Roadblocks" (5–10 slides or short doc). Agreement on 30-day goals.

Artifacts to create and attach to Welcome Station:
- Workstation Snapshot (template): OS, shell, dotfiles, timezone, VPN notes.
- 14d Wins doc (new hire-authored).
- Starter-issue list with traces to onboarding objectives.
- Quick links block: access tickets, primary Slack channels, runbooks.

Mentor handoff checklist (explicit steps to mark readiness):
- 0: Account/Access: all required systems reachable (list) — pass/fail.
- 1: Dev Flow: can clone, run tests, open PR, and explain CI status — scored 0/1/2 (0 needs help; 2 independent).
- 2: Domain context: can summarize product problem area in two sentences.
- 3: Operational awareness: knows where runbooks/pager logs live and how to escalate.
- 4: Social integration: completed 3 async intro interactions across teams.
Notes: mentor should record a one-paragraph assessment in the Welcome Station and recommend either: Keep pace / Slow down onboarding / Move to level-2 tasks.

Competency map (short list used for day-14 calibration):
- Technical craft: repo fluency, test discipline, deployment touchpoints.
- Product sense: problem framing, customer empathy.
- Systems thinking: basic architecture mapping and DB access patterns.
- Reliability orientation: alerting, postmortem mindset.
Scoring bands: Emerging / Developing / Independent (use these words in the day-14 note).

Interview rubric (condensed — for fast hiring calibration):
- Role-fit (weight 20%): clarity of past work, alignment with role outcomes (0–5).
- Technical (weight 45%): problem decomposition, code clarity, tradeoffs (0–10).
- Systems/design (weight 15%): architecture thinking, scaling tradeoffs (0–5).
- Behavioral (weight 10%): collaboration examples, conflict handling (0–3).
- Signals (weight 10%): curiosity, learning growth examples, open-source contributions (0–3).
Decision threshold: normalized weighted score >= 70% = strong hire; 60–69% = hire with manager calibration; <60% = decline.
Quick interviewer notes (what to write into scorecard):
- One-sentence hire rationale, top-3 risks, 30-day success signal.

Offer and acceptance quick playbook:
- Time-to-offer target: 48 business hours after final interview.
- Include: role summary, manager name, first-day link to Welcome Station, mentor name.
- Proposed perks/relocation note (if applicable).
- If remote and hardware delayed: provide stipend for temporary compute (policy code: HR-STIP-007).

Unresolved / open questions (notes to self):
- Should we gate day-2 PR on infrastructure readiness? (tradeoff speed vs reliability).
- Localized onboarding for APAC timezone hires: rotate mentor slots to avoid midnight meetings.
- Evaluate whether 14 days is enough to detect reliability orientation — propose 30-day deep-check.

Appendix: templates + links (placeholders)
- Welcome Station template: link -> CONFLUENCE-ONBOARD-1842
- Workstation snapshot template: link -> gitlab.com/redwood/platform-setup/blob/main/onboard/workstation.md
- Starter-issue backlog: JIRA-HIRE-712 (filter: label=welcome-starter)

Quick edit log (notes):
- 2025-02-12: initial draft (Priya)
- 2025-02-18: added mentor handoff rubric (Evan)
- 2025-02-26: small language edits and remote-first rituals added (Marisol)

Notes to reviewer:
- This doc intentionally favors brevity and copy-paste templates. Please call out missing local compliance steps for private deployments hires (security/team-specific).
summary: Compact 14-day onboarding playbook designed for hybrid/remote hires. Combines daily micro-tasks, mentor handoff signals, a short interview rubric for calibration, and quick offer guidance. For People Ops and managers to copy into a per-hire Welcome Station.
